main_body: Small farm stall/hut: a large tiled roof slope (rows 1-21) over a log-plank wall with a dark door and an inset window (rows 24-35), a lighter porch ledge (rows 36-37), and two legs down to row 43.
top_band: Roof slope in orange and plum tile tones from rows 3 to 21 (L about 120-147 at x=21), closed by a darker eave line at row 21 and a dark shadow at rows 22-23
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above with a tile pattern, and it is clearly separated from the wall below. The eave is marked by a darker row at 21 and a dark shadow band at rows 22-23. The wall has an inset door and an inset window with a dark inner frame, and a lighter ledge at rows 36-37 sits over legs. The roof is a plain rectangle without a ridge, but it still reads as a top slope, like the reference stall roof. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The candidate has 37 median colours per tile, against 18 and 11 for the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown or plum next to the wood and roof. The roof has several tile tones with highlights, and the wall has plank grain, dark joints and an inset window. The roof pattern is repetitive and slightly noisy, but it is as rich as the references and not sticker-like.
